title: Monte Cristo Sandwiches
subtitle: Ham and turkey dipped in egg batter, griddled, and dusted with powdered sugar.
description: Ham and cheese sandwiches dipped in egg batter, griddled golden, dusted with powdered sugar. Serve with jam — sweet-savory hall brunch energy.

ingredients.name: Dijon mustard
ingredients.notes: spread thin on half the slices

ingredients.name: large eggs
ingredients.notes: whisked with 1 cup milk and pinch of salt

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Monte Cristo Sandwiches in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Use sliced deli ham as listed — measure each before heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Eggs. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Build the sandwiches
steps.instruction: Layer ham, turkey, and Swiss between bread slices with a thin smear of Dijon. Press gently and set aside while the griddle heats. Cook until char marks are visible and the thickest piece reads 165°F on an instant-read thermometer. Plan about 12 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Set the dip station
steps.instruction: Whisk eggs and milk in a shallow pan wide enough to fit a sandwich. Heat a large griddle over medium and melt butter until foaming.

steps.title: Dip and griddle
steps.instruction: Dip each sandwich briefly in egg batter—don't soak or bread falls apart. Griddle 3–4 minutes per side until deep golden and cheese melts.

steps.title: Hold and slice
steps.instruction: Transfer to a wire rack in a 200°F oven between batches. Slice diagonally before serving so jam dipping is easier. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Dust and serve
steps.instruction: Dust lightly with powdered sugar through a fine sieve—go easy so it doesn't clump. Serve with warm raspberry jam for dipping at the line.

stationWorkflow: Build all sandwiches before dipping so the griddle never waits for assembly mid-batch.
Keep batter shallow and replace when it gets thick with bread crumbs for clean dips.
Dust sugar at the line, not in the oven—steam makes powdered sugar disappear on held sandwiches.
cleanupNotes: Wipe the griddle between batches to prevent burnt egg batter from scorching the next sandwich.
Wash the dip pan immediately; egg-milk residue glues to stainless once it dries.
leftovers: Reheat sliced halves on a dry griddle over medium-low until cheese remelts and crust re-crisp.
Turn leftover halves into a savory bread pudding by cubing, adding custard, and baking at 350°F.

tonightSpread: Plate Monte Cristo Sandwiches with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Keep hot items on one side of the table and cold on the other — eggs stay hot, fruit stays cold.
Line up Monte Cristo Sandwiches on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
